recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. recommended.title: A verdict that discusses the placeholder rule is not a placeholder
recommended.acceptance: A judgement gate's evidence can DISCUSS the rule that guards it without being refused by it. THE DEFECT, OBSERVED ON THE FIRST REAL USE OF PL-AI-0012 AND NOT PREDICTED. gpt-architect's round-84 verdict approving PL-AI-0012 lists, among its accepted properties, that filler wording does not become a valid judgement merely because the evidence is long -- and it names that wording using the very token the rejected-substring net matches. Transcribing the verdict faithfully was therefore REFUSED by the rule the verdict was approving. The gate was recorded with that one token reworded and the refusal disclosed in the evidence, which is a workaround and not a fix. THIS IS THE FIFTH TIME THIS REPOSITORY HAS PAID FOR THE SAME SHAPE, and that history is the argument for fixing it properly rather than trimming the word list: PL-0701's import guard failed on its own header comment naming the symbol it forbade; PW-0101's no-runtime-switch test failed on its own comment naming the environment variable; PW-0402 failed twice, once on an identifier that contained a forbidden word and once on a text window that reached into the code below it. Every one was a guard matching prose ABOUT the thing rather than the thing. REQUIRED: the rejected-substring net stops firing on a judgement that merely mentions the vocabulary. The implementer chooses the mechanism and must defend it; a shorter word list is NOT a defence, because the next verdict will discuss whichever words remain. The two shapes worth weighing are scoping the net by length -- a placeholding string is short by nature, and evidence long enough to argue about the rule is not one -- and exempting quoted or clearly-cited spans. Whatever is chosen, say in the module why the OTHER one was not. REQUIRED: the net keeps catching what it was built for. The round-83 string, and a real sha followed by wording that says the judgement has not been made yet, must both still be refused, and both already have regressions in scenario 10u that must stay green. REQUIRED: a new regression records THIS incident -- a long, faithful verdict that names the rejected vocabulary while approving a task, accepted; the short string that is nothing but that vocabulary, refused. REQUIRED: the commit-naming rule is untouched. It is the actual rule; the substring list is a second net and the policy note already says so. Nothing here may weaken the requirement that a verdict names the commit it judged. NOT IN SCOPE: the judgementCommitVerified behaviour, which gpt-architect approved as implemented in round 84 with an explicit instruction that it must not become a blanket refusal outside git.
recommended.notes: Filed in round 84 by claude-lead, immediately after PL-AI-0012 was approved and while recording that very approval. NOT one of the two defects gpt-architect ruled must stay inside PL-AI-0012 -- those are advance-completable self-attribution and the harness helper, both manifestations of the authority defect and both repaired there. This is a separate, newly observed defect in the second-net heuristic, found after the reviewed sha. It is filed rather than patched into PL-AI-0012 because that task is approved at 94dd10e and reopening an approved surface to refine a heuristic would invalidate a verdict for no safety gain. P2 because the workaround is a reworded token and the actual rule -- naming the commit judged -- is unaffected.
